epithet: The one people who believed in time
lede: Pharaoh said “I believe” with the sea closing over him, and was told: Now? The people of Yūnus saw the punishment gathering above them, believed, and were spared — the only town of which that is told. Between those two the surah puts its question to Makkah: “Is it a wonder to people that We have revealed to a man from among them?”

names.name: Yūnus
names.note: After the people of Yūnus, mentioned in a single ayah near its end (10:98). The prophet himself appears nowhere else in the surah.

revelation.detail: ʿAṭiyyah and Ibn Abī Ṭalḥah relate from Ibn ʿAbbās that it is Makkan, and so said al-Ḥasan and ʿIkrimah; al-Qurṭubī adds ʿAṭāʾ and Jābir. Reports except two or three ayat as Madinan, usually those beginning “If you are in doubt” (10:94). It opens a run in the muṣḥaf: five surahs that begin with the letters Alif Lām Rā, the first three of them named after prophets. Of the people it is named for, Qatādah said: this was granted to no community that believed as the punishment descended, except the people of Yūnus. The traditional order places it fifty-first, followed directly by Hūd and Yūsuf.

evidence.quote: رَوى عَطِيَّةُ، وابْنُ أبِي طَلْحَةَ عَنِ ابْنِ عَبّاسٍ أنَّها مَكِّيَّةٌ، وبِهِ قالَ الحَسَنُ، وعِكْرِمَةُ
مَكِّيَّةٌ فِي قَوْلِ الْحَسَنِ وَعِكْرِمَةَ وَعَطَاءٍ وَجَابِرٍ
وقالَ قَتادَةُ: لَمْ يَكُنْ هَذا لِأُمَّةٍ آمَنَتْ عِنْدَ نُزُولِ العَذابِ، إلّا لِقَوْمِ يُونُسَ

setting: The objection in Makkah had taken a particular form by now. It was no longer only that the message was unwelcome; it was that the messenger was one of them. A man they had watched grow up, with no kingdom and no following, was saying that the Lord of the worlds had spoken to him. The surah opens on exactly that: “Is it a wonder to people that We have revealed to a man from among them: warn mankind, and give good news to those who believe?”

They had a counter-offer. “Bring a Qurʾan other than this, or change it.” The answer is one of the plainest statements of what revelation is: “Say: it is not for me to change it of my own accord. I follow only what is revealed to me… Had Allah willed, I would not have recited it to you, nor would He have made it known to you. I lived among you a lifetime before it. Will you not reason?” And then the challenge: if he invented it, produce one surah like it, and call on whomever you can.

What is unusual in the surah is how much of it is appeal. “Allah calls to the Abode of Peace.” “For those who do good is the best, and more.” “O mankind, there has come to you an admonition from your Lord, and a healing for what is in the breasts, and guidance, and mercy for the believers. Say: in the bounty of Allah and in His mercy — in that let them rejoice; it is better than what they gather.” It describes how people actually behave: calling on Allah lying down, sitting and standing when harm touches them, and walking on when it is lifted as though they had never called; praying in earnest on a ship in a storm, and forgetting on the shore.

The stories come late and are kept short. Nūḥ, standing alone against his people. Mūsā and Hārūn — and at the end of that story, something told in this way only here. Pharaoh, drowning, says: “I believe that there is no god but He in whom the Children of Israel believe.” The reply: “Now — when you had disobeyed before?” His body is cast up as a sign.

Then one ayah about a people on the Tigris. “Why was there not a single town that believed, so that its faith profited it — except the people of Yūnus? When they believed, We lifted from them the punishment of disgrace in this life.” Quraysh are being shown both doors. And the Prophet ﷺ is told what he may not do about which one they take: “Had your Lord willed, all who are on the earth would have believed, together. Would you then compel people until they become believers?”
aim: To confront those who deny the revelation with arguments and proofs, and to call them to faith by both hope and fear.
themes: Revelation to “a man from among them”
The challenge of a single surah
Man in distress and in ease
A healing for what is in the breasts

outline.title: A man from among them
outline.summary: Alif Lām Rā. These are the ayat of the wise Book. Is it a wonder to people that We have revealed to a man from among them? Your Lord is Allah, who created the heavens and the earth in six days, then rose over the Throne, directing the affair. He made the sun a radiance and the moon a light, and measured out its stations. Those who believe and do right — their call in the gardens of bliss is “Glory be to You, O Allah,” their greeting is “Peace,” and the close of their call: “Praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds.”

outline.title: “Change it”
outline.summary: When harm touches man he calls on Us, lying on his side, sitting or standing; and when We remove it he passes on as though he had never called on Us. Those who do not expect to meet Us say: “Bring a Qurʾan other than this, or change it.” Say: it is not for me to change it of my own accord. I lived among you a lifetime before it. He it is who carries you by land and sea: when a storm wind comes and the waves from every side, they call on Allah, sincere to Him in religion — and when He saves them, they transgress in the land.

outline.title: This life, and the Abode of Peace
outline.summary: The likeness of the life of this world is as water We send down from the sky: the earth takes on its ornament, and its people think they have power over it — then Our command comes by night or by day. Allah calls to the Abode of Peace. For those who do good is the best, and more (10:26). Say: who provides for you from the sky and the earth? Who owns hearing and sight? They will say, “Allah.” What is there after the truth but error? Most of them follow nothing but conjecture.

outline.title: It could not have been invented
outline.summary: This Qurʾan could not have been devised by any but Allah. Do they say, “He has invented it”? Say: then bring a surah like it, and call on whomever you can besides Allah. No — they have denied what they could not encompass in knowledge. Among them are those who listen to you; but can you make the deaf hear? For every community there is a messenger. They say, “When is this promise?” Say: I have no power over harm or benefit for myself, except what Allah wills.

outline.title: A healing, and the friends of Allah
outline.summary: O mankind, there has come to you an admonition from your Lord, a healing for what is in the breasts, guidance and mercy. Say: in the bounty of Allah and His mercy — in that let them rejoice. You are not engaged in any matter, nor do you recite any of the Qurʾan, but We are witness over you; not an atom’s weight escapes your Lord. Truly, the friends of Allah — no fear is upon them, nor do they grieve: those who believe and are mindful. For them is good news in this life and the next. Let not their words grieve you: all might belongs to Allah.

outline.title: Nūḥ, Mūsā and Pharaoh
outline.summary: Recite to them the story of Nūḥ: “My people, if my standing here is hard on you — then resolve on your plan, you and your partners, and give me no respite.” Then We sent Mūsā and Hārūn to Pharaoh. “Whatever you have brought is sorcery; Allah will bring it to nothing.” None believed Mūsā but some youths of his people. “Our Lord, do not make us a trial for the wrongdoing people.” We brought the Children of Israel across the sea. When drowning overtook him he said: “I believe.” — “Now? Today We shall save you in your body, that you may be a sign for those after you.”

outline.title: The people of Yūnus, and the last word
outline.summary: If you are in doubt about what We have sent down to you, ask those who read the Book before you. Why was there not a town that believed, so that its faith profited it — except the people of Yūnus? Would you compel people until they become believers? Say: look at what is in the heavens and the earth. Say: O mankind, if you are in doubt about my religion — I worship Allah, who takes your souls. If Allah touches you with harm, none can remove it but He. Follow what is revealed to you, and be patient until Allah judges.

keyAyah.why: The surah’s description of the Qurʾan, addressed to everyone: an admonition, a healing, a guidance and a mercy — the thing the next ayah says to rejoice in.

virtues.text: “When the people of the Garden have entered the Garden, Allah, blessed and exalted, will say: ‘Do you wish for anything more that I should give you?’ They will say: ‘Have You not made our faces bright? Have You not admitted us to the Garden and saved us from the Fire?’ Then He will lift the veil; and they will have been given nothing dearer to them than looking upon their Lord.” Then he recited: “For those who do good is the best, and more.”
virtues.arabic: فَمَا أُعْطُوا شَيْئًا أَحَبَّ إِلَيْهِمْ مِنَ النَّظَرِ إِلَى رَبِّهِمْ

virtues.text: ʿUbādah ibn al-Ṣāmit asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about “For them is good news in the life of this world.” He said: “It is the righteous dream, which the believer sees, or which is seen for him.”

“When Allah drowned Pharaoh, he said: ‘I believe that there is no god but He in whom the Children of Israel believe.’ Jibrīl said: ‘Muḥammad, if only you had seen me taking the mud of the sea and thrusting it into his mouth, for fear that mercy would reach him.’”

before: Al-Tawbah closed: “There has come to you a Messenger from among yourselves.” Yūnus opens with the people who found precisely that hard to accept: “a man from among them.”
after: Yūnus tells its stories briefly, and names a people who were spared. Hūd tells the same stories at length — and none of the peoples in it were.
